title: NCCL symmetric window registration fails 4096-byte alignment when collective memory uses a separate BFC allocator
body:
Buffers that XLA assigns to the collective memory space can fail NCCL symmetric window registration (`ncclCommWindowRegister`). NCCL requires the window base address to be aligned to 4096 bytes (`NCCL_WIN_REQUIRED_ALIGNMENT`), but when collective memory is served by a separate BFC allocator, allocation bases are only 256-byte granular. The separate allocator is used with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=cuda_async`, with `--xla_gpu_enable_allocator_spatial_partitioning=false`, or with `preallocate=false`. There is no flag workaround. The failure depends on BFC chunk placement, and two Mosaic-GPU collective kernels per executable make it deterministic for us.

## Context

We are porting an expert-parallel MoE dispatch/combine transport to a full training step, one process per GPU. The transport is a multi-process Pallas Mosaic-GPU kernel that writes peer buffers directly through `plgpu.remote_ref` and device semaphores. XLA therefore places the kernel's buffers in the collective memory space and registers them as NCCL windows. We use the separate-allocator configuration to work around an unrelated window-exhaustion problem with the default spatially partitioned pool, which we will file separately.

## Repro

Run a program with two multi-process Pallas Mosaic-GPU collective kernels per executable, on ≥ 2 processes with one process per GPU, with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=cuda_async`. Our kernel and multi-process harness are public: [`put_segments`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/marin-ep-8081/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/_moe/marin_ep_transport.py) with the smoke [`smoke_mgpu_train_multiproc.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/marin-ep-8081/experiments/marin_ep/bench/smoke_mgpu_train_multiproc.py). The smoke's docstring lists the env vars. Four 1-GPU processes on one GB200 node suffice. We are happy to reduce this to a standalone script.

### Actual

Registration of the second kernel's buffers fails:

```
dev_runtime.cc:881 (ncclDevrWindowRegisterInGroup) NCCL WARN Window address must be suitably aligned.
INTERNAL: NCCL operation nccl_status failed: invalid argument
```

`TF_CPP_VMODULE=nccl_symmetric_memory=3` shows the failing window at a 256-granular offset (for example `0x…300`) inside the collective memory region.

### Expected

Allocations in the collective memory space meet the alignment that NCCL window registration requires. The default spatially partitioned pool already guarantees this by aligning to the collective memory granularity (2 MiB).

## Root cause hypothesis

XLA registers one window per `BufferAllocation` base ([nccl_symmetric_memory.cc#L88-L92](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/60f8069e8b/xla/backends/gpu/collectives/nccl_symmetric_memory.cc#L88-L92)). When the default BFC pool serves collective memory via spatial partitioning, the allocator entry sets `min_alignment` to the collective memory granularity ([se_gpu_pjrt_client.cc#L1472-L1489](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/60f8069e8b/xla/pjrt/gpu/se_gpu_pjrt_client.cc#L1472-L1489)). The `CreateCollectiveBFCAllocator` entry [sets no `min_alignment`](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/60f8069e8b/xla/pjrt/gpu/se_gpu_pjrt_client.cc#L1579-L1592). PR #44156 removed an earlier size-rounding for collective buffers, on the premise that allocators configure per-memory-space alignment. This allocator entry never did.

## Fix validation

We rebuilt `jax-cuda13-pjrt` at jax `8d1be7d7` / xla `60f8069e` with one change: `BFCAllocator::RoundedBytes` rounds request sizes to 4096. The failure is gone at 8 ranks (2 nodes) and at 64 ranks (one NVL72 rack, 25/25 training steps, outputs numerically conformant against a reference path). The rounding is a blunt instrument. Setting `min_alignment` on the allocator entry looks like the intended mechanism, but we validated only the rounding variant. Also observed: raising `kMinAllocationBits` to 12 instead trips the `BinForSize(bin_size) == BinFromIndex(b)` construction invariant.

## Environment

- GB200 NVL72, CUDA 13. The failure reproduces on one node with 4 GPUs, one process per GPU.
- jax/jaxlib/plugin/pjrt `0.11.1.dev20260809` and `.dev20260816` nightlies, NCCL 2.30.7
- Analyzed at xla `60f8069e8b`. The code paths above are unchanged at `f0bfd165e0` (2026-08-17).
- Related: #47283 (`kMaxPeers` bound in the multi-GPU barrier kernel, same campaign). Two further issues affect Mosaic-GPU collective kernels but have flag workarounds: window registrations exhaust NCCL's per-rank window space under the default allocator configuration, and dynamic-slice fusion drops the collective memory space from buffers of fused kernels. We will file both separately.
